items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And thanks to John Wilson, he wrote a really good review.

ctx.x: [laughs, claps] Well, let‟s go back, you said the first jazz recording you heard was Teddy Wilson. Teddy Wilson is improvising. Up until this point, had you even improvised? Had you even …?

Yes. No, I prac— I had to take from records. I had to take the solo and song, because I didn‟t know any songs. So solos, and I tried to play that solo. It doesn‟t make any difference, especially when I was in Fukuoka, I took a solo, from eight bars, you know, Wilson‟s solos, things like that, everybody‟s. And then I tried to play it on the piano.
So you were transcribing, or just by ear memorizing and then playing, transposing to piano?
